messages.subject: boxplot problem
parts:
Dear ggplot2 user,

I have a problem with the y-axis in boxplot.

Please see the first plot (natural.png).  My data has a long tail, so I only plotted through 50.  Note that the mean for the red group is about 14, for green group about 8, and about 10 for the blue group.

Because I want to show the data has a long tail, so I opt to plot with log transformation of the y-axis.  Please see (log transformation.png).  It looks very nice since it shows the whole data.  However, the mean values all seem off. 

The code for generating both graphs are very similar.  The only difference is for the natural.png, I used "scale_y_continuous(limits=c(1,50), drop=FALSE, breaks=breaks, lables=breaks)+", for the log transformation one, I used "scale_y_log10(breaks = breaks, labels=breaks)+".

What could have caused the problem?

Thanks,
Xi

messages.author: 20a8e3faa83e8923
messages.subject: Re: boxplot problem
parts:
Xi,

the ylim statement is the problem! ylim on its own subsets the data. That means that the boxplots you have are boxplots of the data only up to 50 - which changes the mean values as you described.
You can use coord_cartesian to 'zoom into' the plot:

x=rep(1:2,1000)

y=rnorm(2000, mean=45, sd=20)

qplot(x, y, group=x, geom="boxplot")

qplot(x, y, group=x, geom="boxplot") + ylim(c(0,50)) # subset

qplot(x, y, group=x, geom="boxplot") + coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0,50)) #zoom


HTH,

Heike
